coverage: Read the underlined heading and both exercise references, opening assumptions, both lines of (Et), every word and formula in items 1–4, all crossed-out/overprinted words and symbols, every handwritten digit/sign/bracket, all source margins and bottom-left archive number. Both halves were viewed once after one whole-page view. Seven unique tight crops were each viewed once. No part remains unviewed. H supplies only an editorial description and was not collated as source text.

changes.locus: Condition (Et), composition between u and v
changes.evidence: Crop 01 shows a small round closed contour low beside the u and v, ending near their baseline; the exact round glyph remains circle/o. Lowered placement is recorded without construing it as a mathematical index.
Crop 01 has curved upper and lower lobes with an inward middle stroke and curled right endpoints; this settles the epsilon-shaped type. The second typed relation has the same visible shape in half a.

Crop 02 shows a rounded lower bowl, a hooked upper contour and a middle stroke. These favour epsilon, but the reinforced crossing strokes do not eliminate membership; the same two candidates are retained in revised order.

changes.locus: Item 2 opening, superscript on the Prol domain S(X)
changes.evidence: Crop 03 shows one short descending stroke joined at a low vertex to a longer rising stroke. There is no initial crest; the codomain sign in the same crop does have an initial crest and trough.
changes.mathematical_consequence: The written vee is preserved even though the context suggests the topos notation used elsewhere; no normalization or proof check was made.

changes.locus: Item 2 g display, cancelled strokes beneath slash
changes.evidence: Crop 04 places the small overwritten u/m-like strokes below the slash, with the live slash above and to their left. The reading keeps both layers and the existing u/m doubt.

changes.locus: Item 2 remainder, circle between g and f
changes.evidence: Half a and its overlap with half b show the small closed round mark low between g and f; it repeats the low circular glyph whose first occurrence is marked uncertain.

changes.locus: Item 2 final formula, circle between f and g
changes.evidence: Half b shows the small closed round mark low between f and g, matching the recurring low circular form; first-occurrence circle/o uncertainty is retained in (Et).
Crop 05 exposes a lowercase p descender and bottom serif beneath a capital P with its taller stem and upper bowl. Both letters are visible; the ink does not establish their order of striking.
Crop 06 clearly shows a comma head and descending curved tail superposed at the middle m stem. Plain munie alone omits visible ink. The relative order of comma and m remains uncertain.

Crop 07 confirms an acute above the r slot as well as the following é. In the r slot a curved lower return and middle trace suggest an é/r superposition; the order is not recoverable, and the accented-r reading is retained as a visible alternative.

c_doubts.evidence: Crop 01: two rounded lobes and inward middle stroke settle the epsilon-shaped glyph, independently of membership meaning.
Crop 01: crossed pen strokes contain m/M-like humps; case cannot be separated from cancellation.
Crop 02: rounded bowls favour epsilon, but the reinforced middle/top strokes also permit membership.
Crop 04: the cancelled lower strokes permit u or m; placement beneath slash is clear.
Crop 06 resolves the presence of a comma; the remaining uncertainty is which character was struck first.
Crop 07 settles the extra acute as present, but the underlying r/é slot and strike order remain uncertain. Unaccented présentation is rejected.
Half b: the word ends n, followed by a clear blank before de; there is no final s.

c_doubts.locus: Item 3 last line, pŕésentation audit duplicate
c_doubts.evidence: Same locus and crop as the preceding spelling doubt: extra acute visible; possible r/é overprint retained, with no second crop.

unresolved.locus: Recurring low round composition glyph; first occurrence in (Et)
unresolved.reason: Closed small round contour near baseline; distinguish low placement from unresolved glyph identity. Later occurrences are unmarked following the first candidate.

unresolved.reason: Rounded epsilon-like contour is reinforced by strokes which also permit membership.

unresolved.locus: Cancelled pen strokes below g-display slash
unresolved.reason: Several joined and crossed strokes prevent secure separation of the underlying small letter.

Comma and m are both visible; strike order is not.
Acute is secure; the extra curved lower trace permits é/r superposition, but an accented r cannot be excluded.

notes.text: Exercice 4.10.7 resumes the hypotheses and notation of Exercice 4.10.6 and adds condition (Et). No date or authorial/typed page number appears; the bottom-left 11 is treated as the archive sheet number.
notes.basis: Observation: heading, opening and whole-page margins.

notes.text: The condition is written with composable u and v and three epsilon/membership-shaped relations to underlined M. The composition is written in u-then-v order. The first typed relation is epsilon-shaped; the final pen relation remains uncertain. The cancelled word ces and cancelled m/M-like strokes beneath M are retained.
notes.basis: Observation: (Et), half a and crops 01–02. Meaning was only a cue to inspect signs, not a substitute for their shapes.

notes.text: Item 1 asks for base change by u:X→Y to define a site morphism S(u) from S(X) to S(Y), expressed by left exactness of S(u)*. The phrase du topos is visibly cancelled.
notes.basis: Observation: item 1, half a. No proof checking performed.

notes.text: Item 2 asks for left exactness of Prol_X, a morphism g with g*=Prol_X and g_*=Res_X, a retraction of f, and an adjunction morphism id→f◦g. The first displayed-in-line domain superscript is visibly vee-shaped; the other listed topos signs are waves. The id target after g◦f has S(X) without a tilde, as C already records.
notes.basis: Observation: item 2, both halves and crops 03–04. Mathematical expectations prompted scrutiny of the first superscript but were not used to replace its ink.

notes.text: Item 3 asks for failure of the conclusions without (Et), proposing schemes with the f.p.p.f. topology and the reference [S.G.A. 3 IV]. It keeps singular les conclusion. For M it gives flat morphisms of finite presentation after cancelling fidèlement. Initial-letter superpositions and the final extra acute are retained with visible alternatives.
notes.basis: Observation: item 3, half b and crops 05–07. The counterexample was read, not mathematically established.

notes.text: Item 4 reads Acheter une médaille en chocolat pour les rédacteurs. No diagram, drawing, insertion pointer, date or further marginal text was found beyond the archive number.
notes.basis: Observation: final item and all four margins in the whole and lower-half views.

notes.text: H is a description-only witness on this scan, so no H collation rows were created. Pen numerals, stars, tildes/slashes, brackets and corrections are visibly present, but their writer is not identified by this reading. This was transcription inspection only: no targeted proof, re-proof, computation, formal certificate or background-result recheck was performed.
